I paid $38 for this used mechanical keyboard, and honestly, I think I got about $38 worth of keyboard. Maybe a little more.

Let's start with the flaws. The space bar rattles. Not a gentle click, but a hollow, loose clatter every time my thumb hits it, like a tray of cutlery being nudged. I've stopped noticing it during the day, but late at night it sounds louder than it has any right to. The "E" key also occasionally repeats itself, so "meeting" sometimes becomes "meeeting." It happens maybe once every few paragraphs, which is just often enough to keep me proofreading.

Communication with the seller was slow. I asked what switches it used before buying, and the reply came a full week later, after the keyboard had already arrived. (Brown switches, for the record.)

Still, here's the surprising part: it's genuinely comfortable. The keys have a satisfying, cushioned feel, and I can write long emails without my wrists complaining. That's more than I can say for the flat laptop keyboard I was using before.

I considered shipping it back, but the hassle didn't seem worth it. So it stays on my desk, rattling, repeating, and quietly earning its keep.

Three stars.

Thirty-eight bucks. That's what I paid, and honestly, that number explains most of how I feel about this keyboard.

Let's get the bad stuff out of the way. The space bar rattles. Not a gentle clack, either. It's a loose, tinny sound, like a spoon in an empty drawer. And the J key repeats sometimes, just often enough that I've typed "jjust" in three separate emails to my landlord, who probably thinks I'm losing it.

I asked the seller what switches it had before I bought it. He answered a week later. A *week*. By then the thing was already on my desk and I'd figured out they were browns by pulling a keycap and squinting. His reply was one word: "brown." Thanks, man.

But here's the thing. I write long emails for work, the kind that go on forever, and this keyboard is genuinely comfortable for that. My wrists don't ache by the end of the day. The keys have this soft little bump that makes typing feel almost pleasant.

So I kept it. Shipping it back would've eaten a chunk of what I paid, and I'd rather just live with the rattle. Three and a half stars.
